paragraphs.source_en: To his disbelief, Fuwa Kawachi-no-kami had come for a fourth time. This time he would undoubtedly speak of Oichi and the children. Nagamasa ground his teeth in hatred. Oichi and the children had resolved to die in Odani Castle with him and his father, and Nagamasa could not bear to unsettle their hearts. Without waiting for the envoy to arrive, he pressed his lips together, took up his sword, and went downstairs.

paragraphs.source_en: He made his way toward the rooms of his wife Oichi and their three daughters. Perhaps this would be their final meeting. Ordinarily the foot of the mountain could be seen from here, but the morning mist made the view unusually dim today. The area around the Kyogoku enclosure, already fallen into enemy hands, glowed crimson as though ablaze, and Nagamasa stopped in his tracks. The flames kindled by the victorious Oda army were painfully bright amid the morning mist.
